notes: Three university-layer documents (academic integrity policy, AI guidelines, syllabus template); both coders marked all three delegates. Main disagreements on matched units: (1) phase for institutional training/support commitments (A over-time, B before-course): resolved to before-course as institutional set-up; for the syllabus-statement recommendation resolved to course-start; for 'only permitted once you have practiced essential skills' resolved to during-work; for exclusive-AI assessment resolved to during-assessment. (2) actor on rationale text in the syllabus samples and on the committee-adoption sentence (A instructor/admin, B student/all): resolved to the addressee, i.e. student for second-person sample text and all for the adoption statement. (3) unit_stance (the largest group): 'encouraged to prepare guidelines' units are neutral, 'encouraged to explore uses of AI' is encourage, 'some but not all assignments' is restrict, verification duties are neutral, sanctions are neutral. (4) policy_type: one real disagreement, the make-up option in the sanction list (A P68, B P37), resolved to P68 with a one-rule policy; the hallucination-free tool criterion (A P65, B UNCOVERED) resolved to UNCOVERED. (5) modality: advice 'rather than AI detection software' resolved to should-not; dean's discretionary powers to may. Alignment: sentences that A and B coded as separate rules in the same passage (Dean's Designee review vs Provost record keeping; fabrication definition vs 'refrain from using AI-generated output as data') were left unmatched and both kept. One-coder units were checked against the source and kept (17 A, 9 B) when they stated a rule or consequence. Dropped: B's integrity-policy introduction sentence (no AI content, no rule) and A's duplicate P41 coding of the 'early studies' sentence already covered by the P55 unit. B's merged policies (notice plus evidence, penalty plus make-up, approval plus detector advice) were split or trimmed to one rule per unit. Counts: only_A and only_B include the dropped units.
